Class LobbyManager

java.lang.Object
network.server.core.LobbyManager
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable, LobbyCommandVisitor
public class LobbyManager extends Object implements Runnable, LobbyCommandVisitor
Central registry and manager for every client session on the server. It owns, and is the sole mutator of, three maps:
  • connectedPlayers — every connected player, keyed by name;
  • lobbies — lobbies still waiting to fill up;
  • activeGames — players in a running game, each mapped to its GameController.

Threading model — single-thread actor (mirror of GameController)

The LobbyManager owns one BlockingQueue of LobbyCommand and one daemon lobby-thread that drains it in run() via cmd.accept(this). Every map mutation happens on that thread, so the maps are plain HashMap/LinkedHashMap with no locks. The sole exception is shutdown(), which first joins the lobby-thread so it becomes the only accessor before clearing the maps.

Network endpoints never invoke the visit(...) handlers directly; they enqueue commands through an API — submit(LobbyCommand) for menu commands and onDisconnect(String) for disconnections — and return at once. The callers are GameServerRemoteImpl and SocketClientHandler (incoming commands) and the per-player LivenessSentinels (liveness timeouts).

Player registration is the only synchronous path and uses an "ask" pattern: submitSocketRegistration(String, Socket, ObjectInputStream, ObjectOutputStream) / submitRmiRegistration(PlayerEntry) enqueue a registration command and return a CompletableFuture that the lobby-thread completes with the verdict (accept/reject). The duplicate-name check (nameAlreadyTaken(String)) and the reservation (connectedPlayers.put) run back-to-back on the lobby-thread with no blocking call between them, and each command is handled run-to-completion before the next is dequeued: the queue's serialization is the mutual exclusion. A second attempt on the same name therefore always observes the first one's reservation, so two attempts can never both win.

No blocking work on the lobby-thread

Blocking socket-handshake I/O lives in ConnectionHandshaker, on the per-connection thread. The only residual blocking calls — view.close() (drains a player's sender) and controller.shutdown() (joins a game-thread) — are handed off to a dedicated single-thread executor (shutdown-executor) so the lobby-thread returns to the queue immediately. It never reads or writes the game model. When a lifecycle event affects a running session (disconnect, reconnect, leave-after-game-over) it enqueues the matching LobbyCommand on that session's queue and returns; the model is mutated only by the GameController's game-thread.

    • shutdownExecutor

      private final ExecutorService shutdownExecutor
      Off-loads the only blocking calls the lobby-thread would otherwise make: VirtualView.close() (drains a player's sender) and GameController.shutdown() (joins a game-thread). Each is a wait on a local thread — no network, no foreign lock — but running it inline would stall the command queue, so it is delegated here. Single-thread, daemon, named shutdown-executor.

    • submitSocketRegistration

      public CompletableFuture<Boolean> submitSocketRegistration(String playerName, Socket socket, ObjectInputStream in, ObjectOutputStream out)
      Submits a socket player for registration on the queue ("ask" pattern) and returns a future carrying the verdict. The view, handler and reader thread are built by the lobby-thread only if the name is free (see visit(RegisterSocketPlayerCommand)), so a rejected attempt allocates nothing.
      Parameters:
      playerName - the requested name
      socket - the live client socket (used to build the view if accepted)
      in - the handshake input stream, reused as the command reader
      out - the handshake output stream, reused for outbound messages
      Returns:
      a future completed with true (accepted, reader already started) or false (rejected, name already taken)

    • submitRmiRegistration

      public CompletableFuture<Boolean> submitRmiRegistration(PlayerEntry entry)
      Submits an already-built RMI PlayerEntry for registration ("ask" pattern). This path is leaner than the socket one: the entry and its RmiVirtualView are already constructed by the caller, so the lobby-thread has no view/handler to build and no client-<name> reader thread to start (RMI dispatch is driven by the runtime, not by a reader loop). There is also no blocking handshake I/O to off-load to the shutdown-executor, and the RmiVirtualView allocates no network resources until activateLiveness(), so a rejected name leaks nothing. The lobby-thread's work thus collapses to the name check plus a single map put (or a reject).
      Parameters:
      entry - the RMI player entry created by GameServerRemoteImpl
      Returns:
      a future completed with true (accepted) or false (rejected, name already taken)

    • run

      public void run()
      Lobby-thread loop: take one command and dispatch it via accept(this). A handler exception is logged but never kills the thread; an interrupt ends the loop cleanly. Mirrors GameController.run().

      run in interface Runnable

    • visit

      public void visit(RegisterSocketPlayerCommand cmd)
      Atomic check-and-register for a socket player. If the name is free it builds the view, handler and entry, registers the player and starts the client-<name> reader thread, then completes the future with true; otherwise it completes with false. All of this is non-blocking and the lobby-thread performs no I/O. Construction happens only after the name check, so a rejected name allocates no instances. The future is always completed — even if construction throws — so the handshaker never blocks until its timeout.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - the socket-registration request: requested name, the live socket and its streams, and the verdict future to complete

    • visit

      public void visit(RegisterRmiPlayerCommand cmd)
      Atomic check-and-register for an RMI player. The PlayerEntry is already built and RMI has no reader thread, so this only registers the player (or rejects a duplicate name) and completes the future. As above, the future is always completed.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - the RMI-registration request: requested name, the prebuilt PlayerEntry, and the verdict future to complete

    • visit

      public void visit(CreateLobbyCommand cmd)
      Handles a create-lobby request. Sends the player an error and returns if they are already in a game, already in a lobby, or asked for a size outside the allowed 2–5 range. Otherwise, it creates the lobby, adds the player, and refreshes the lobby list for browsing players.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - request to create a new lobby

    • visit

      public void visit(JoinLobbyCommand cmd)
      Handles a join-lobby request. Sends the player an error and returns if they are already in a game or a lobby, or if the target lobby is missing or full. Otherwise, it adds them and, if that fills the lobby, starts the game (see startIfFull(Lobby)). The browsers' lobby list is refreshed either way.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - request to join an existing lobby

    • visit

      public void visit(LeaveCommand cmd)
      Handles a leave request, branching on the player's state:
      • in a finished game (END_OF_GAME): forwards the command to the session queue (the controller cleans up the model), removes the entry from activeGames, and — once no connected player remains in that session — drops any leftover (disconnected) entries and shuts the controller down, off-loading the blocking join to shutdown-executor;
      • in a lobby (pre-game): handled locally by handleLeaveFromLobby(String) (the model is not touched);
      • in game or browsing: an error is sent back to the player.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - voluntary leave from a lobby or a finished game

    • visit

      public void visit(LobbyDisconnectCommand cmd)
      Disconnect teardown, run on the lobby-thread. If the player was in a running game it enqueues a PlayerDisconnectedCommand on that session's queue (the controller handles disconnection/suspension). It then removes the player from connectedPlayers and closes their view (the blocking close is off-loaded to shutdown-executor), and finally removes them from any hosting lobby — dropping the lobby if empty and refreshing the browsers.
      Specified by:
      visit in interface LobbyCommandVisitor
      Parameters:
      cmd - server-internal disconnection request, enqueued by the liveness sentinels and the transport handlers

    • shutdown

      public void shutdown()
      Orderly shutdown, invoked from a ServerMain JVM hook (a different thread). Stops and joins the lobby-thread first so this thread becomes the sole accessor of the maps, then shuts every active GameController down, closes all outbound views, clears the maps and stops the shutdown-executor. The instance is unusable afterwards.
